problems.stem: Which item belongs in a realistic maintenance plan for a personal portfolio site?
options: A promise to redesign the entire site every week
A recurring quarterly check to update the resume PDF, swap in the newest project, and test that all links still resolve
Nothing; a published site never needs attention
Deleting the site after one month so it cannot go stale
problems.explanation: Maintenance is small and recurring: refresh content, add new work, and re-test links on a set cadence. Weekly redesigns and never touching it are both unrealistic.

problems.stem: Six months after launch, a visitor clicks your Projects link and gets a 404 because you renamed the file. What maintenance practice would have caught this?
options: A periodic link check (manual click-through or a link-checker tool) listed in the maintenance plan
problems.explanation: Renaming or moving files breaks internal links. A scheduled link check, manual or automated, is the maintenance step that catches broken paths before visitors do.

problems.stem: You ask an AI to generate a maintenance checklist. It includes 'renew your SSL certificate monthly' and 'update server dependencies.' Your site is a static GitHub Pages site. What is the right response?
options: Follow all items literally; the AI knows best
Drop the items that do not apply to static GitHub Pages (it manages HTTPS and has no server dependencies) and keep the items that do, like content and link checks
Stop using GitHub Pages because it cannot do those things
Add even more server tasks to be safe
problems.explanation: A generic AI checklist assumes a server you do not run. GitHub Pages handles HTTPS automatically and has no dependencies to patch, so you keep only the items that fit a static site.

problems.stem: Which maintenance-plan entry is specific enough to actually act on later?
options: On the first of each quarter: replace the oldest project card, refresh resume.pdf, and click every nav and project link
Update when I feel like it
problems.explanation: An actionable plan names the trigger (first of each quarter) and the exact tasks. Vague intentions like sometime or make it good cannot be verified or repeated.
